chunks: Abu Abdillah al-Husayn ibn Ahmad ibn Muhammad ibn Ahmad al-Ashnani al-Darimi, the Jurist, the Just, in Balkh, narrated to us, saying: My grandfather informed me, saying: Muhammad ibn Ammar narrated to us, saying: Musa ibn Isma'il narrated to us, saying: Hammad ibn Salama narrated from Muhammad ibn Ishaq, from Muhammad ibn Ibrahim al-Tamimi, from Salama, from Abu al-Tufayl, from Ali ibn Abi Talib (peace be upon him),

that the Messenger of Allah (peace be upon him and his Family) said: O Ali, indeed for you is a treasure in Paradise, and you are its Man with Two Horns. Do not follow one look by another look in prayer, for indeed, the first is (permitted) for you, whereas the other is not (permitted) for you.
ai.seo_question: What is the meaning of 'Dhu al-Qarnayn' in relation to Imam Ali and the ruling on looking during prayer?
ai.summary: This hadith from Shaykh al-Saduq’s *Ma'ani al-Akhbar* highlights Ali ibn Abi Talib’s unique spiritual status by linking him to the Quranic figure Dhu al-Qarnayn, a title signifying his dominion over the two worlds or his dual leadership of the faithful and the righteous. The Prophet’s instruction on prayer etiquette—permitting the first glance but prohibiting the second—serves as a practical lesson in maintaining khushu’ (focus) and guarding against distraction, reflecting the broader Shia emphasis on the purity of worship. This narration underscores Ali’s role as the exemplar of both spiritual authority and meticulous adherence to prophetic tradition.

en.basel-kadem: 1.	We were told by Abu Abdillah, Hussain bin Ahmad bin Muhammed bin Ahmad al-Ishnani al-Darimi, the Jurist, the Just, in Balkh, that he said: I was told by my father, that he said: We were told by Muhammed bin Ammar, that he said: We were told by Musa bin Isma’il, that he said: We were told by Hammad bin Salama, from Muhammed bin Ishaq, from Muhammed bin Ibrahim al-Taimi, from Salama, from Abu’l-Tufail, from Ali bin Abi Talib, peace be upon him,

that the Messenger of Allah, Allah’s blessings be upon him and his Family, said: O Ali, indeed, for you is a treasure in Paradise, and you are its Man with Two Horns. Do not follow one look by another look in prayer, for indeed, the first is (permitted) for you, whereas the other is not (permitted) for you.
